title: Paged block allocator for KV cache with thermal-aware GPU page swapping
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: Implement a paged/blocked KV cache allocator that reduces OOMs and p99 token latency under oversubscription by aligning KV allocations to GPU-friendly blocks, supporting staged swap buffers, and introducing a thermal-aware swap policy that cooperates with continuous batching.

Problem statement: Current KV cache uses a simple slab allocator that fragments memory under mixed-length sequences and variable batch concurrency. When active sequences exceed physical GPU residency we experience high swap churn and burst p99 increases. Existing tickets (ENG-33412, ENG-31240) explored sharded scheduling and atomic swap orchestration but left open the allocator-level layout, prefetch strategy, and how to incorporate GPU telemetry (temperature/SM utilization) into swap decisions.

Proposal summary: Build a paged block allocator which: 1) divides each model KV region into fixed 'blocks' (configurable 64KB-1MB depending on model and GPU page sizes) with per-block residency metadata; 2) maintains LRU+cost heuristics at block granularity instead of per-kv-entry; 3) exposes cooperative hints to the batching layer to prefer grouping requests with contiguous block affinity; 4) implements a swap path using pinned host staging buffers + async peer-to-peer transfers where available; 5) integrates a thermal-aware swap damping factor: as GPU temperature or SM saturation rises, aggressive prefetching and large swaps are throttled in favor of smaller targeted migrations to protect latency and hardware thermal headroom.

Key components: allocator metadata table (compact bitmap + epoch), block residency manager (resident, staged, swapped), swap engine (async cudaMemcpy/GPUDirect or NIC-based RDMA where available), prefetch adviser (batch-aware hints), and an observability surface (per-block metrics, swap-rate, avg-residency, batch-affinity misses).

Why block granularity: Blocks reduce metadata churn (bitmap fits L2 cache better than per-entry maps), let us align allocations to GPU kernel page sizes (reduces fragmented VRAM waste), and enable batching to reuse proximate KV blocks within the same inflight microbatch.

Thermal-aware swapping rationale: High swap throughput can increase SM contention and thermal throttling, which degrades latency SLOs. We will sample temperature and SM occupancy counters and compute a throttle multiplier in the swap engine. When multiplier < 1, the engine prefers eviction of cold blocks and defers large prefetch windows. This keeps p99 stable under long running heavy workloads (e.g., real-time chat ingestion).

Compatibility & fallbacks: The allocator supports: (a) GPU local pages only; (b) pinned-host staging buffers with zero-copy where supported; (c) pure host-swap fallback for older instances. A runtime flag will allow disabling thermal damping for benchmarking.

Documentation/Artifacts: design doc on Confluence link, perf microbench harness, and integration PRs are referenced below.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator divides KV regions into configurable blocks and exposes block-level residency API
Swap engine performs async GPU<->host transfers using pinned buffers and avoids blocking critical warp paths
Batching layer can request block-affinity hints and scheduler shows measurable reduction in cross-block fetches in perf tests
End-to-end benchmarks show <=5% increase in token throughput for resident-heavy workloads and >=25% reduction in swap churn for oversubscribed traces compared to baseline
p99 generation latency under representative oversubscription workload is improved or stable compared to baseline when thermal damping is enabled
Comprehensive metrics added: swap_rate, block_residency, prefetch_miss_rate, swap_latency_p50_p95_p99, gpu_temp_trace linked to swap events
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike implemented - prototype block allocator + simple LRU eviction tested on small model (7B). Observed 18% reduction in fragmentation vs slab baseline. - Jun

2026-03-04: Added pinned staging buffer path and async memcpy; initial microbench shows host-swap latency median 2.4ms for 256KB blocks on p4d. Need to validate on A100 nodes for PCIe vs NVLink behaviour. - Aisha

2026-03-06: Design review notes from Tomas Ortega: ask to add safety margin for CUDA OOMs, and to expose a per-model block size tuning parameter. Also suggested more granular metrics for batch-affinity misses. Action: add tuning config and extra metrics. - Review

2026-03-08: Implemented thermal damping factor using NVML temperature and SM utilization. On high temp traces, swap throughput reduced by 30% and p99 improved by 22% in synthetic tests. Need real workload validation and to ensure damping does not starve memory for hot requests. - Jun

2026-03-10: Integration tests added into CI. Failing test discovered: race between batch scheduler hint revocation and block eviction leading to stale prefetches. Mitigation: introduce per-block epoch and fast revocation token. Working on fix. - Aisha
design_decisions: Block size default chosen as 256KB for mid-size and 1MB for large models; empirical sweet spot balances metadata overhead vs swap granularity
LRU+cost heuristic: cost = estimated refrequency * block_size_penalty + last_access_age; avoids evicting small hot fragments inside a block
Use pinned host staging for best portability and GPUDirect paths where available; avoids requiring host-visible unified memory in customer infra
Thermal damping uses an exponential backoff multiplier derived from NVML temp delta and SM utilization; simpler throttle preferred over complex ML-based predictors for predictability
Prefetch strategy is batch-affinity first: prefetch contiguous neighbors up to N blocks or until budget exhausted; N is adaptive based on recent hit-rate
tests: Unit: allocator APIs, block bitmap correctness, epoch revocation logic
Integration: simulate mixed-length sequences with continuous batching to validate prefetch hints reduce cross-block fetches
Perf: run replicated token-generation traces used in infra-benchmarks; compare swap rates, p50/p95/p99 token latency between baseline and new allocator
Fault: force OOM at specific allocation points to validate fast fallback to host-swap and safe rollback of in-progress prefetches
Long-run: 72h soak with synthetic chat workload to surface thermal and swap-stability regressions
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag: kv.paged_allocator.enable
Stage 1 (canary): 5% of traffic on dedicated staging cluster with identical model versions; collect block-level metrics and heatmaps
Stage 2 (ramp): 25% with thermal damping enabled; monitor p99, swap_rate, and GPU temp correlation
Stage 3 (full): 100% after 2 weeks of stable metrics and no regressions; enable auto-tuning of block size for models with stable patterns
Rollback: runtime flag off and a quick migrate path to reconstruct per-entry slab metadata from block snapshots (fast path less than 30s)
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on race conditions between batch scheduler and eviction; see progress update 2026-03-10
Validate thermal damping parameters on A100 vs V100; sensor sampling rate is currently 500ms - we may need to tune
Check that pinned buffer pool size is bounded to avoid host OOM; current default pool = 4GB per node
Review metrics coverage: need per-model tag support for block_residency and swap_rate
